introduction.value: Claude pulls up to 150 active Redfin listings via a scraper, computes median price per square foot, and flags below-median listings with long days on market for investors. Tutorial, not a confirmed first-person account.

method.value: The Redfin Scraper actor is added to Claude as an MCP tool using an Apify token. The investor describes the search in plain language, covering metro, budget and minimum beds. Claude calls the scraper for up to 150 active listings and computes median price per square foot. It then flags listings at least 15% below that median with above-average days on market. The post suggests sold comps as a follow-up check.

outcome.value: In the post's example, Claude pulled 142 listings, found a $312 median per square foot, and flagged six candidates. This is an illustrative walkthrough, not a reported real run. It ranks listings as cheap only relative to other active listings.

notes.value: The post says a 150-listing pull costs about $0.09 to $0.15. A weekly scheduled version across three metros runs under $2 a month, and sold comps are needed to confirm a listing is truly underpriced.

source_text.body:
Source motivated-seller real estate deals from Redfin listings
Claude pulls up to 150 active Redfin listings via a scraper, computes median price per square foot, and flags below-median listings with long days on market for investors. Tutorial, not a confirmed first-person account.
Done with
CL
Claude
What they did
The Redfin Scraper actor is added to Claude as an MCP tool using an Apify token. The investor describes the search in plain language, covering metro, budget and minimum beds. Claude calls the scraper for up to 150 active listings and computes median price per square foot. It then flags listings at least 15% below that median with above-average days on market. The post suggests sold comps as a follow-up check.
How it went
In the post's example, Claude pulled 142 listings, found a $312 median per square foot, and flagged six candidates. This is an illustrative walkthrough, not a reported real run. It ranks listings as cheap only relative to other active listings.
Worth knowing
The post says a 150-listing pull costs about $0.09 to $0.15. A weekly scheduled version across three metros runs under $2 a month, and sold comps are needed to confirm a listing is truly underpriced.
Try it yourself
with
Claude
Copy prompt
Here is a list of up to [150] active real estate listings in [city or zip code] with price, square footage, and days on market: [paste data or attach file]. Calculate the median price per square foot, then flag listings priced below that median that have been on the market more than [60] days. Give me a ranked table of the flagged listings with the reasons they look like motivated sellers, and note any listings with missing data you had to skip.
Original source: https://themineworks.com/blog/real-estate-investor-deal-sourcing-pipeline/
